QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_1

question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil, a Chartered Accountant empanelled as a Social Impact Assessor with ICAI, is briefing a newly-registered NPO (Pragati Foundation) about the regulatory character of the Social Stock Exchange in India. Which of the following statements MOST accurately captures the legal status of the SSE as defined under the SEBI ICDR Regulations, 2018?

answer.text: The SSE is a standalone, independently incorporated stock exchange operating under its own SEBI recognition certificate, separate from NSE and BSE.
The SSE is a separate segment of a recognised stock exchange having nationwide trading terminals, permitted to register NPOs and FPEs to list their securities.
The SSE is a private matchmaking platform run by ICAI that connects donors to NPOs without any SEBI supervision.
The SSE is a sub-platform of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs' MCA21 portal that serves as a donor-NPO directory only.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook p.52 and the SEBI ICDR Regulations, the SSE is a separate segment of a recognised stock exchange having nationwide trading terminals, permitted to register NPOs and FPEs to list their securities. It is not a standalone exchange. The Trap: Option A conflates a segment with a standalone exchange — a common error that inflates the SSE's institutional footprint. Option C confuses the SRO role of ICAI with exchange operation. Option D invents a non-existent link between MCA21 and the SSE. Note: The 'separate segment' framing is what allows the SSE to leverage existing recognised stock exchange infrastructure rather than building a new exchange from scratch.
